item.title: CERN and Mistral partner to build AI foundation models for physics
item.description: European physics research centre CERN and Mistral AI have signed a statement of intent to establish a long-term strategic partnership to develop foundation models for scientific discovery, the two organisations said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: European physics research centre CERN and Mistral AI have signed a statement of intent to establish a long-term strategic partnership to develop foundation models for scientific discovery, the two organisations said on Thursday. The partners aim to build a "Large Physics Model", which CERN said in a statement would be the first foundation model for collider physics, trained on billions of simulated particle collisions. It is meant to replace some specialised algorithms now used to reconstruct and identify particles. CERN holds about one exabyte, or one million terabytes, of experimental data from the Large Hadron Collider, and expects the volume of collisions to increase tenfold after its ongoing upgrade, expected around 2030. "High-energy physics provides a unique environment in which artificial intelligence can be developed and tested with exceptional rigour," CERN Chief Information Officer Enrica Porcari said. No timeline or budget was disclosed. Both sides said the models could later serve other sciences.

item.title: What is the 'hospital of the popes' where Leo is recovering from surgery?
item.description: Rome's Gemelli Hospital has become the preferred medical facility for modern pontiffs since the time of Pope John Paul II.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Rome's Gemelli Hospital, where Pope Leo is [USN:L8N4610IA TEXT:"recovering after surgery"] for [USN:L8N46006S TEXT:"lung cancer"], is known as the "hospital of the popes". The hospital, with a suite especially for popes, has become the preferred medical facility for modern pontiffs since the time of Pope John Paul II. WHAT IS THE GEMELLI? Located some 5 km (3 miles) from the Vatican City, the Gemelli hospital offers every major medical speciality under one roof. It also serves as the teaching hospital of the Catholic University of the Sacred Heart and has more than 1,600 beds. There is a dedicated suite for popes on the 10th floor, including a private chapel. However, this is currently under renovation, meaning Leo is staying in a different set of rooms. In the 2026 Newsweek-Statista "World's Best Hospitals" rankings, Gemelli was named as Italy's top hospital and ranked 33rd globally among more than 2,500 hospitals assessed across 32 countries. HOW DID IT BECOME THE POPES' HOSPITAL? Popes were traditionally treated by doctors summoned to their residence. For example, Pope Paul VI underwent prostate surgery in 1967 in a specially equipped operating room set up inside the Vatican's Apostolic Palace. Everything changed during the pontificate of John Paul II. He was rushed to the Gemelli after a 1981 assassination attempt, undergoing emergency surgery that saved his life. He returned repeatedly to the hospital over the following decades for treatment, spending more than 150 days there during his pontificate. He dubbed the place "Vatican III", after the official residences at the Vatican itself and Castel Gandolfo. Benedict XVI was never admitted during his pontificate. By contrast, Francis, who died in April 2025, was hospitalised several times, including for colon surgery in 2021, respiratory problems and abdominal surgery in 2023, and for bilateral pneumonia in the weeks before his death. IS GEMELLI OWNED BY THE VATICAN? The Gemelli hospital was built on land originally owned by the Vatican that was donated by Pope Pius XI in 1934 to the body that oversees the Catholic University. Opened in 1964, it is named after Agostino Gemelli, the Franciscan friar, physician and psychologist who founded the university. However, despite its close association with the papacy, Gemelli is not a Vatican institution. It operates as a private non-profit academic medical centre within Italy's healthcare system, with most patients treated through the country's publicly funded health service. The Vatican owns the Bambino Gesù hospital in Rome, but that facility specialises in paediatric care.

item.title: La china ByteDance crea equipo de seguridad de IA, inicia campaña de contratación a nivel mundial
item.description: Seed, la unidad de investigación en IA del gigante tecnológico chino ByteDance, creó un equipo de "Alineación y Preparación" y ha puesto en marcha una campaña global para contratar a 10 investigadores, afirmando que realizará una inversión a largo plazo en la seguridad de la IA para sus modelos, cada vez más capaces.
item.dc:creator: Eduardo Baptista
item.content:encoded: Seed, la unidad de investigación en IA del gigante tecnológico chino ByteDance, creó un equipo de "Alineación y Preparación" y ha puesto en marcha una campaña global para contratar a 10 investigadores, afirmando que realizará una inversión a largo plazo en la seguridad de la IA para sus modelos, cada vez más capaces. Esta campaña de contratación se produce en un momento en el que crece el escrutinio sobre la seguridad de los agentes de IA tanto en China como en Estados Unidos, especialmente ahora que los desarrolladores les otorgan autonomía para acceder a Internet. La "alineación de la IA" se refiere a los esfuerzos por garantizar que los sistemas avanzados de IA actúen en consonancia con los objetivos humanos y los requisitos de seguridad, sobre todo al llevar a cabo tareas complejas que constan de varios pasos. El anuncio de ByteDance constituye una de las pocas veces en que un importante desarrollador chino de IA ha hecho pública una iniciativa específica centrada en la seguridad de los modelos de vanguardia, la alineación y la preparación ante riesgos emergentes. El periódico The Paper, respaldado por el Estado, informó el martes que Seed fue el primer laboratorio chino de IA de vanguardia en crear un departamento independiente de seguridad y alineación. Esta medida se produce además en medio de un debate más amplio entre Estados Unidos y China sobre las medidas de control de la IA, los riesgos de seguridad y los canales de comunicación para informar sobre incidentes importantes relacionados con la IA, incluso mientras ambos países compiten por el liderazgo en el sector. A medida que mejoran las capacidades de los modelos, la seguridad y la alineación ya no son simplemente medidas de protección frente al riesgo, sino capacidades fundamentales que determinarán si los modelos pueden implementarse a gran escala, afirmó Seed en una oferta de empleo publicada el miércoles en su cuenta oficial de WeChat. Seed afirmó que proporcionaría al nuevo equipo una capacidad informática y unos recursos de investigación comparables a los de que disponen los equipos dedicados a los modelos de vanguardia. Los puestos se ubicarán en Pekín, Shanghái y San José, California. Su investigación incluirá formación en seguridad en todas las etapas del desarrollo de modelos, pruebas automatizadas de vulnerabilidades, herramientas para supervisar y explicar el comportamiento de los modelos, entornos de prueba de agentes de IA y preparativos para riesgos emergentes. Seed afirmó que también buscaría realizar pruebas independientes y colaboraría con universidades e instituciones de investigación, aplicando la investigación en materia de seguridad al entrenamiento, la evaluación y el despliegue de los modelos.

item.title: China's central bank chief urges 'comprehensive' view on global imbalances
item.description: China's central bank governor called for looking beyond current account and exchange rate adjustments when it comes to global imbalances, in a further defence of China's policies against trade partners' criticisms.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: China's central bank governor called for looking beyond current account and exchange rate adjustments when it comes to global imbalances, in a further defence of China's policies against trade partners' criticisms. The People's Bank of China (PBOC) Governor Pan Gongsheng urged a "more comprehensive analytical perspective" regarding global imbalances in a G20 meeting of finance ministers and central bank governors on Thursday in Bangkok, a central bank statement showed. Pan said attention should be paid not only to the current account, which covers goods and services trade, but also to money flows in financial channels, according to the statement. Global imbalances cannot be resolved through exchange rate adjustments alone, he said. Deficit and surplus countries should work in concert to achieve a dynamic equilibrium in the global economy, Pan was quoted as saying. As China's trade surplus [USN:L6N4600GE TEXT:"surges"], European leaders have intensified calls for a stronger yuan. The PBOC [USN:L6N45U0ON TEXT:"pushed back"] against foreign criticism of its exchange-rate policy in a statement earlier this month, saying it neither needs nor intends to obtain a trade competitive edge through exchange-rate depreciation.

item.title: Indian central bank issues clarifications on FX hedging curbs

item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Reserve Bank of India on Thursday issued clarifications on its latest policy measures to support the rupee, following concerns about tighter hedging rules and cash margins on certain derivatives used to protect against a weaker rupee. The RBI has announced a series of measures since October 10, including redirecting oil companies' dollar purchases to a special facility and levying cash reserve requirements on FX hedges for import liabilities and banks' own assets and liabilities. The measures sparked unintended consequences, with several lenders holding back on quoting dollar-rupee forwards due to confusion over which transactions the cash margin requirement would be levied on.

item.title: Turkey to account for 20% of Europe-CIS new aircraft demand over 20 years, Airbus says
item.description: Airbus expects Turkey to account for about 20% of demand for new passenger aircraft in Europe and the CIS over the next 20 years, requiring 1,800 new aircraft as passenger traffic grows, a senior Airbus executive said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Airbus (AIR.PA) expects Turkey to account for about 20% of demand for new passenger aircraft in Europe and the CIS over the next 20 years, requiring 1,800 new aircraft as passenger traffic grows, a senior Airbus executive said on Thursday. Antonio Da Costa, Airbus vice president for market analysis and forecast, said the number of flights taken annually per person in Turkey was expected to triple to 3.1 by 2045, surpassing the regional average of 2.4. "We expect to see the need for Turkey as a whole, 1,800 new aircraft to renew the fleet and especially grow at the rate that's expected," Da Costa said, adding that passenger traffic in Turkey was expected to grow by around 4.5% annually over the next 20 years, compared with 2.9% for the wider region. "Our expectation is that the fleet of aircraft in Turkey overall, throughout all the airlines, will more than double over the next 20 years," Da Costa said. According to Airbus' latest Global Market Forecast, Europe and the CIS region will need 8,190 new passenger aircraft by 2045, including 3,600 for growth and 4,590 for fleet renewal. Da Costa said Istanbul's position as an international connecting hub continued to strengthen, driven by strong tourism demand and transit traffic. Asked about the impact of the conflict in the Middle East on aviation demand, Da Costa said Turkey had benefited from traffic diversions away from parts of the Gulf region, attracting more tourists and connecting passengers. "We do see an opportunity... there's more incoming tourists and more connecting passengers coming through Turkey due to the conflict in the Gulf," he said. While expecting regional tensions to ease over time, Da Costa said he believed the additional traffic flowing through Turkey would support the country's longer-term growth.

item.title: Italy's political risks cloud debt reduction hopes amid bond turmoil
item.description: Italy's national election next year throws doubt on Rome's plans to reverse the rise in its huge public debt, analysts say, warning that the strong market appetite for Italian bonds in recent years may be coming to an end.
item.dc:creator: Sara Rossi, Valentina Consiglio
item.content:encoded: Italy's national election next year throws doubt on Rome's plans to reverse the rise in its huge public debt, analysts say, warning that the strong market appetite for Italian bonds in recent years may be coming to an end. Italy's €3-trillion ($3.36 trillion) government bond market, one of the world's biggest, has come under renewed scrutiny amid contagion from a sharp selloff in French debt, while domestic political uncertainty mounts and the boost from European Union post-COVID recovery funds fades. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni has followed a largely prudent fiscal policy, but with her rightist coalition trailing the centre-left in opinion polls, she will be under pressure to open the purse strings [USN:L8N45U0SU TEXT:"ahead of next year's vote"], analysts say. "We expect fiscal risk premia to continue to build ahead of the election," Filippo Taddei, Senior European Economist at Goldman Sachs, told Reuters. ITALIAN YIELD SPREAD WIDENS Recent weakness in Italian bonds has been driven by the selloff in France, [USN:L8N45U1VY TEXT:"where a weakened government is trying to pass a budget"] and a key election looms next year, but focus is also turning to Italy's political complications. The yield on the 10-year bonds (BTPs) of the euro zone's third-largest economy hit 4.7% this month and the yield gap with safe-haven Bunds - a market gauge of the risk premium investors demand to hold Italian debt - reached its widest in almost 18 months. The BTP yield has risen more than 100 basis points so far this year and is set for the biggest annual jump since 2022, when an inflation surge sparked a rise in interest rates. [USN:L8N45O0PD TEXT:"Swiss bank UBS"] has recommended that investors go short BTPs, forecasting that the Bund-BTP spread, which was as narrow as 60 basis points in January, will widen to 150 bps. It currently stands at around 105. A short position is a bet that an asset will weaken in price. Goldman Sachs' Taddei said Italy's debt-to-GDP ratio, which climbed to 136.7% in 2025, will remain on a rising path at least until 2028, and warned that if 10-year BTP yields remain above 4% the debt will continue to increase in future years. Higher bond yields mean higher debt-servicing costs. Italian interest spending exceeded €100 billion last year, while average issuance costs rose to 3% in September from 2.75% a year earlier, Treasury data showed. DEFICIT TO FALL - THEN RISE The government has targeted the budget deficit to fall this year to 2.9% of gross domestic product, just inside the EU's 3% ceiling, [USN:L8N45O0R5 TEXT:"only to rise back above 3%"] in the next two years in order to hike defence spending and tackle surging energy costs. The picture is not all bleak, however. Growth held up better than expected in the first two quarters and the government this month hiked its full-year 2026 growth forecast to 1% from 0.6%, thanks in large measure to billions of euros of EU post-COVID funds which have lifted investments. With EU payments under the programme due to end by December, TS Lombard global macro director Davide Oneglia said the country now needed structural reforms, not just fiscal caution. "Meloni doesn't have a big plan for the economy," he said at a TS Lombard conference last week in London. "Not rocking the boat is not enough and her own political stability is not certain." Ratings agency Moody's, which a year ago upgraded Italy's sovereign rating to "Baa2" from "Baa3", raised similar concerns in a new report last week. "Slower growth, reduced fiscal discipline or weaker reform momentum would put the projected debt reduction trajectory at risk," it said. ($1 = 0.8937 euros)

item.title: US wants Senegal debt restructuring wrapped up in less than a year
item.description: The United States views Senegal's request for debt restructuring as a "great example" of progress on the Group of 20 Common Framework, and wants to see work on the case completed in less than a year, a top US Treasury official said on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Andrea Shalal
item.content:encoded: The United States views Senegal's request for debt restructuring as a "great example" of progress on the Group of 20 Common Framework, and wants to see work on the case completed in less than a year, a top US Treasury official said on Thursday. Erin Browne, Treasury undersecretary for international affairs, co-chaired a [USN:L8N4601AF TEXT:"meeting of the Global Sovereign Debt Roundtable"] on Wednesday together with the heads of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank. The group, which also includes creditors, borrowers and private sector players, released its progress report on the sidelines of the IMF-World Bank annual meetings in Bangkok. It was set up to help speed up treatments under the Common Framework following protracted processes in Zambia and Ghana. "We've made really good progress in terms of the sovereign debt architecture, particularly with sovereign debt restructurings," Browne told Reuters in an interview. "We highlight Senegal as a great example of moving forward under the [USN:L6N4570JZ TEXT:"Common Framework sovereign debt restructuring"]." Senegal is in the midst of a debt treatment that aims to return its finances to a sustainable trajectory. "We want this done quickly, transparently, and as expeditiously as possible, so that while there's not a clear timeline ... some in the room were saying in less than one year, and I think that that's a goal that we should all be aiming for," Browne said. IMF Managing Director [USN:S0N43A00E TEXT:"Kristalina Georgieva"] on Wednesday also expressed optimism that Senegal would be able to renegotiate its debts, and said the IMF would support Senegal with a staff-negotiated agreement for a $2.2 billion program. Browne said the debt roundtable included robust conversation about expanding which countries could seek debt treatments, beyond the poorest countries initially included. Discussions on that issue would continue next year, Browne said, adding that participants had not discussed names of specific countries at Wednesday's meeting. Browne said Thursday's meeting of G20 finance ministers went well, touching on issues such as global imbalances, modernizing the global financial system, including through streamlining regulations, and global sovereign debt issues, as well as financial literacy.

item.title: US 10-year Treasury yield levels not unprecedented, BNY CEO says
item.description: The levels the benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield has touched this year are not unprecedented, the CEO of the oldest US bank told Reuters, as a bruising selloff in government debt lifted yields to multi-decade highs.
item.dc:creator: Saeed Azhar, Arasu Basil
item.content:encoded: The levels the benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield has touched this year are not unprecedented, the CEO of the oldest US bank (BNY.N) told Reuters, as a [USN:L1N45V0NY TEXT:"bruising selloff in government debt"] lifted yields to multi-decade highs. The 10-year US Treasury yield, a yardstick for global borrowing costs and asset prices, posted its [USN:L8N45N0KW TEXT:"sharpest rise since 1994"] in the July-September period. "We got 10-year rates to like, call it five and a quarter. There's nothing particularly unusual in history about 10-year rates at that level. We've had arguably low levels for a very long time," BNY CEO Robin Vince told Reuters on Thursday. "People get very caught up. It has happened quickly, for sure, but with what I would view as more of a normalization of the curve." BNY's profit applicable to common shareholders jumped 20% to $1.61 billion, or $2.34 per share, in the three months ended September 30, driven by interest income growth and stronger market levels that boosted the value of client assets. Assets under custody and administration rose 10% to $63.4 trillion in the reported quarter from a year earlier. Global bond markets have come under intense pressure this year as energy prices remain elevated, while the AI boom is supporting economic growth, a combination that has heightened worries about inflation and rising interest rates. "You can make a good case that it is actually the strength of the US economy that's one of the primary drivers of inflation and the move higher in rates," Vince said. A surge in [USN:L1N44D06H TEXT:"debt issuance to fund the artificial intelligence buildout"] has also contributed to the upswing in bond yields. "There's just more debt in the world. There need to be buyers for that. The supply and demand is going to put upward pressure," Vince said. [USN:L6N460140 TEXT:"This week's rout in AI stocks"] has, however, eased some pressure on the beaten-down bond markets, with investors flocking to safe-haven government debt in the face of the tech selloff, pushing US yields down across the curve. The 10-year Treasury yield was [USN:L8N4610QB TEXT:"headed for the largest one-day decline"] since early August 2025 on Thursday. Asked about the AI trade and the infrastructure buildout, Vince said he would be surprised if there were a glut based on what's been built out so far. "Will we need the product that those data centers are producing? Will we have a glut? I think the answer is we will need them," Vince said. [USN:L1N3I80VH TEXT:"BNY has grown into the world's largest custodian"]. The company sits at the center of global capital markets, safeguarding and administering trillions of dollars in client assets, while processing trades and moving securities and cash between financial institutions. DEPOSITS EXPECTED TO PICK UP IN Q4 In a statement, Vince said that client demand is continuing to grow and BNY's sales and pipelines remain very healthy across products and regions. Average deposits are expected to pick up in the fourth quarter along with client activity, Chief Financial Officer Dermot McDonogh told Reuters. The New York-based firm is also benefiting from a rise in interest rates as it reinvests cash from maturing investment securities at higher yields. Net interest income — the spread between earnings from assets and costs on liabilities — accounts for roughly 25% of BNY's revenue, McDonogh said.

item.title: Lufthansa está em negociações para comprar os 50,1% restantes das ações da TAP no futuro, diz CFO
item.description: Estão ocorrendo negociações separadas sobre a possibilidade de a Lufthansa adquirir, no futuro, os 50,1% restantes da participação majoritária na companhia aérea portuguesa TAP, afirmou nesta quinta-feira o diretor financeiro da Lufthansa.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Estão ocorrendo negociações separadas sobre a possibilidade de a Lufthansa (LHAG.DE) adquirir, no futuro, os 50,1% restantes da participação majoritária na companhia aérea portuguesa TAP, afirmou nesta quinta-feira o diretor financeiro da Lufthansa. Nesse processo, o governo português poderia se tornar acionista da Lufthansa com uma participação de até 5%, disse o diretor financeiro Till Streichert. Na quarta-feira, o governo português escolheu a Lufthansa para adquirir uma participação de até 49,9% na TAP Air Portugal por 1,2 bilhão de euros (US$1,35 bilhão), em detrimento da rival Air France-KLM (AIRF.PA) . O negócio, que vem sendo negociado há anos e sofreu repetidos atrasos, é o próximo passo na consolidação do setor aéreo europeu. Streichert disse que espera que o negócio seja fechado no primeiro semestre de 2028 e gere 450 milhões de euros em sinergias. O presidente-executivo da Lufthansa, Carsten Spohr, disse aos jornalistas que o negócio era “uma combinação perfeita” para o grupo. A Lufthansa já é proprietária da Austrian Airlines, da ITA Airways e da SWISS, entre outras companhias aéreas. Ele disse que seria uma transação mais fácil de ser aprovada pela União Europeia do que a da italiana ITA, cuja reestruturação ainda está em andamento, já que há menos sobreposição de negócios com a Lufthansa. (Reportagem de Klaus Lauer)

item.title: EU-backed east Mediterranean undersea cable project applies to resume seabed research, Greece says
item.description: Greece said on Thursday the developer of an EU-backed undersea power cable scheme in the eastern Mediterranean has applied for a licence to resume seabed surveying, key for the long-delayed project to move ahead.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Greece said on Thursday the developer of an EU-backed undersea power cable scheme in the eastern Mediterranean has applied for a licence to resume seabed surveying, key for the long-delayed project to move ahead. Construction of the Great Sea Interconnector (GSI) aims to link the European mainland to Cyprus and later Israel, but is opposed by Turkey. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio in Athens last week said the US was [USN:L6N45U0PA TEXT:""very committed""] to the project as it promotes energy supply diversification, necessary due to Russia's war in Ukraine and the situation in the Strait of Hormuz. Greece's power grid operator IPTO (ADMr.AT) is developing the €1.9 billion ($2.13 billion) scheme. French company Nexans (NEXS.PA) , the cable contractor, has on behalf of the GSI applied for a Greek permit to survey the seabed, Greek government spokesperson Pavlos Marinakis told reporters on Thursday. Progress on the project has been slow amid a dispute between Greece and Turkey over the maritime area that will be designated for laying down the cable. Greece hopes to resume seabed surveying to determine the route soon, a move Turkey says would need prior coordination between the two countries as it crosses an area under a 2019 maritime deal with Libya, which Athens has rejected. Marinakis said surveying will be carried out by a French ship and would start after a Greek ministerial committee in charge of permitting marine research in Greek maritime zones and the Greek coast guard approve the request. "With regards to the project implementation, Greece has not made arrangements with the authorities of any state other than France and Cyprus — which is the obvious case," Marinakis said. Rubio said last week that the US will use diplomacy to try to remove any possible hurdles. ($1 = 0.8917 euros)

item.title: La guerre au Moyen-Orient aura un impact durable sur le commerce - directrice OMC
item.description: Les conflits en Ukraine et au Moyen-Orient ainsi que les bouleversements géopolitiques en cours auront un impact durable sur le commerce mondial, a dit jeudi à Reuters Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, directrice générale de l'Organisation mondiale du commerce (OMC).
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Les conflits en Ukraine et au Moyen-Orient ainsi que les bouleversements géopolitiques en cours auront un impact durable sur le commerce mondial, a dit jeudi à Reuters Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, directrice générale de l'Organisation mondiale du commerce (OMC). Au Moyen-Orient, les échanges commerciaux se sont fortement contractés depuis que Etats-Unis et Israël ont déclenché une guerre contre l'Iran fin février - et ce malgré une série de solutions de contournement. Leur reprise prendra du temps, a estimé Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala lors d'une interview en marge des réunions annuelles du Fonds monétaire international et de la Banque mondiale organisées à Bangkok, ajoutant que certains changements pourraient devenir permanents. L'OMC prévoit une baisse de 17% des exportations en provenance du Moyen-Orient cette année et un repli de quelque 15% des importations. Des experts du secteur tablaient au début du conflit sur un retour à la normale des flux commerciaux une fois la guerre terminée et le détroit d'Ormuz rouvert, par lequel transite en temps normal 20% du trafic maritime mondial d'hydrocarbures. Mais, depuis, la durée du conflit a souligné la nécessité d'une diversification et certaines des routes commerciales alternatives devraient perdurer, a poursuivi Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala. "Nous constatons que le monde des doit réfléchir à des goulets d'étranglement (tels que le détroit d'Ormuz)", a-t-elle encore dit. "Je pense que certaines de ces alternatives resteront en place car les pays tout comme les entreprises voudront se prémunir contre toute éventualité", a déclaré la directrice générale de l'OMC. Elle dit ainsi s'attendre à une poursuite voire à une amplification des efforts de diversification vers différents pays. Comme autre choc pesant sur les échanges commerciaux, Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala a cité la multiplication des droits de douane imposés par le président américain Donald Trump depuis son retour au pouvoir en janvier 2025. "Il ne fait absolument aucun doute que les chaînes d'approvisionnement ont été réorganisées," a-t-elle déclaré, ajoutant que les chefs d'entreprise ont fait preuve de créativité pour trouver de nouvelles routes commerciales, avec le bémol qu'elles s'avèrent plus coûteuses. UNE OPPORTUNITÉ POUR LE COMMERCE INTRA-AFRICAIN Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala a également souligné le potentiel de croissance du commerce intra-africain. "Les échanges entre Africains peuvent véritablement créer de la valeur et générer des emplois," a-t-elle déclaré, précisant que le commerce intra-africain représentait désormais environ 20% du commerce africain. A titre de comparaison, les échanges au sein de l'Union européenne représentaient environ 60% du total de ses échanges commerciaux. L'OMC a relevé la semaine dernière ses prévisions de croissance du commerce mondial de marchandises, la demande de produits liés à l'intelligence artificielle (IA) devant compenser l’impact des perturbations provoquées par la guerre au Moyen-Orient. La croissance du volume du commerce mondial de marchandises devrait atteindre 3,9% en 2026, contre un chiffre de +1,9% retenu dans les prévisions de l'OMC publiées en [USN:L6N40712R TEXT:"mars"]. Selon Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, l'avenir reste incertain compte tenu des conflits en cours, des droits de douane et des craintes que l'essor de l'IA ne s'essouffle voire ne retombe. "L'impact de l'IA masque les autres tendances du commerce, qui ne sont pas positives," a-t-elle déclaré.

item.title: Ucrânia retoma ataques a refinarias russas e Zelenskiy critica EUA
item.description: A Ucrânia retomou seus ataques a refinarias russas com um ataque a uma instalação na região de Ryazan, informou o governador regional nesta quinta-feira, depois que o presidente ucraniano Volodymyr Zelenskiy expressou sua indignação com uma “perigosa” retirada dos serviços de inteligência dos EUA.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: A Ucrânia retomou seus ataques a refinarias russas com um ataque a uma instalação na região de Ryazan, informou o governador regional nesta quinta-feira, depois que o presidente ucraniano Volodymyr Zelenskiy expressou sua indignação com uma “perigosa” retirada dos serviços de inteligência dos EUA. Desde o anúncio surpresa do presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, sobre um cessar-fogo energético entre a Rússia e a Ucrânia no domingo, Kiev havia se abstido de ataques às refinarias russas, aos quais o líder norte-americano atribuíra a responsabilidade pelo aumento dos preços do diesel nos mercados globais. Mas Zelenskiy vinha manifestando crescente frustração com os contínuos ataques da Rússia à infraestrutura energética ucraniana, que, segundo ele, deixaram 600 mil pessoas sem energia elétrica na quarta-feira. Ele alertou que a Ucrânia não suspenderia seus próprios ataques indefinidamente se a Rússia não fizesse o mesmo e também criticou o que considerou ser o favoritismo de Trump em relação à Rússia. Em entrevista ao Financial Times publicada na quinta-feira, ele afirmou que a paciência da Ucrânia havia se esgotado. “A restrição (ao ataque a refinarias) acabou. Chega”, disse ele ao jornal. Pavel Malkov, governador de Ryazan, afirmou em uma postagem no Telegram que um grande ataque ucraniano com drones na região havia provocado um incêndio em uma refinaria de petróleo. “Os danos materiais estão sendo avaliados neste momento. As equipes de emergência estão trabalhando no local”, disse ele. Em sua entrevista, Zelenskiy criticou a ânsia de Washington em fechar acordos comerciais com Moscou e a aparente admiração de Trump pelo russo Vladimir Putin. No sábado, Trump pediu que a Ucrânia substituísse Zelenskiy e criticou veementemente os ataques ucranianos à infraestrutura petrolífera russa, um dia após anunciar um acordo de fornecimento de diesel com a Rússia, com o objetivo de reduzir os preços dos combustíveis, que dispararam desde o início da guerra dos EUA e de Israel contra o Irã, em fevereiro. Apesar da suspensão dos ataques a refinarias por parte da Ucrânia, autoridades ucranianas reclamaram que não haviam recebido nenhum alerta antecipado dos EUA nos últimos dias sobre mísseis balísticos russos a caminho. Eles também afirmaram que a versão militar do serviço de comunicações via satélite Starlink, de Elon Musk, teve sua velocidade reduzida em todo o país, prejudicando as operações na linha de frente e os ataques de médio alcance contra alvos militares russos. Musk afirmou na quarta-feira, em uma postagem no X, que o Starshield — a versão militar do Starlink — era de propriedade e controle do governo dos EUA, que decidia sobre quaisquer limites de velocidade. Zelenskiy afirmou que oficiais militares ucranianos foram avisados por seus homólogos norte-americanos de que Washington bloquearia o acesso a informações de inteligência, a menos que suspendessem os ataques à infraestrutura energética russa. Na entrevista ao FT, Zelenskiy disse que a suspensão foi apresentada a Kiev como uma falha técnica, mas descartou a ideia de que as falhas no sistema de satélites Starlink pudessem ter sido causadas por um problema técnico. “Não foi um problema técnico, foi uma decisão deliberada”, disse ele ao FT.

item.title: POINT MARCHÉS Les craintes sur la dette liée à l'IA bousculent à nouveau les Bourses mondiales
item.description: Wall Street est attendue en ordre dispersé et les Bourses européennes évoluent également dans le désordre jeudi à mi-séance, les inquiétudes sur le niveau d'endettement des entreprises liées à l'intelligence artificielle (IA) refaisant surface et poussant les investisseurs vers les valeurs refuge.
item.dc:creator: Diana Mandia
item.content:encoded: Wall Street est attendue en ordre dispersé et les Bourses européennes évoluent également dans le désordre jeudi à mi-séance, les inquiétudes sur le niveau d'endettement des entreprises liées à l'intelligence artificielle (IA) refaisant surface et poussant les investisseurs vers les valeurs refuge. Les futures sur indices new-yorkais signalent une ouverture en hausse de 0,26% pour le Dow Jones (.DJI) , mais en baisse de 0,29% pour le Standard & Poor's-500 (.SPX) et de 1,22% pour le Nasdaq. À Paris, le CAC 40 (.FCHI) prend 0,16% à 7.885,75 points vers 11h14 GMT. À Francfort, le Dax (.GDAXI) recule de 0,47% et à Londres, le FTSE 100 (.FTSE) avance de 0,57%. L'indice EuroStoxx 50 (.STOXX50E) perd 0,88%, le FTSEurofirst 300 (.FTEU3) 0,23% et le Stoxx 600 (.STOXX) 0,25%. Le coût de l'assurance contre les défauts de paiement des géants technologiques américains atteignent jeudi des niveaux record, un nouveau signe des tensions croissantes sur le marché du crédit dans le secteur de l'intelligence artificielle (IA), qui touchent particulièrement les opérateurs de centres de données, dont la rentabilité dépend des revenus futurs. L'un d'entre eux, le groupe américain CoreWeave (CRWV.O) , doit près de 50 milliards de dollars à ses créanciers, selon les données de LSEG, et a chuté mercredi de 15% à la Bourse de New York, ce qui lui a fait perdre un cinquième de sa capitalisation boursière. Le rendement des obligations à échéance 2031 de CoreWeave a bondi jeudi à 16,4%, selon Tradeweb, une plateforme de trading électronique, tandis que le coût de l'assurance contre la dette du groupe a grimpé au-delà de 1.000 points de base pour atteindre des niveaux records, montrent les données de S&P Global Market Intelligence. L'onde de choc sur les marchés du crédit du secteur touche également Oracle (ORCL.N) , Amazon (AMZN.O) , Alphabet (GOOGL.O) , Meta (META.O) et Nvidia (NVDA.O) . L'action CoreWeave et celles des géants de la "tech" américaine devraient continuer à souffrir jeudi, selon les indications en avant-Bourse, et la vague de ventes s'étend, dans le même temps, aux [USN:L6N4610JN TEXT:"marchés européens"] après avoir également touché les asiatiques pendant la nuit. L'indice des nouvelles technologies sur le Stoxx 6000 (.SX8P) recule de 3,08%, après être tombé en séance à son plus bas niveau depuis plus de trois semaines, à 998,99 points. Si les inquiétudes concernant l'endettement élevé du secteur, en pleine course à l'IA, ne sont pas nouvelles, les chiffres de l'inflation américaine du mois de septembre les ont encore exacerbées, car une politique monétaire plus restrictive de la Réserve fédérale (Fed) pour y remédier aurait pour effet d'augmenter les coûts de financement des entreprises. Ces difficultés poussent les investisseurs à se détourner du risque et à se réfugier dans les obligations d'État, ce qui entraîne une hausse de leurs cours et une baisse de leurs rendements, qui avaient récemment atteint des sommets inégalés depuis plus de deux décennies. Les chiffres de l'inflation américaine ont une nouvelle fois bouleversé les anticipations des marchés financiers, qui estiment désormais à 50% la probabilité d'une hausse des taux en octobre, une hypothèse qui avait été écartée ces dernières semaines. Le président de la banque centrale américaine, Kevin Warsh, prendra la parole à Bangkok dans la nuit de jeudi à vendredi à l'occasion de la réunion annuelle du FMI qui se tient dans la capitale thaïlandaise, une dernière occasion d'influencer les anticipations avant la décision de politique monétaire prévue dans moins de deux semaines. La séance du jour est par ailleurs marquée par de nombreux indicateurs économiques aux Etats-Unis, dont les ventes au détail, les inscriptions au chômage et les prix à la production (PPI). LES VALEURS À SUIVRE À WALL STREET [USN:L8N4610PD] VALEURS EN EUROPE Les actions des fabricants européens de puces électroniques et des groupes liés à l'IA chutent fortement jeudi, ASML (ASML.AS) , STMicroelectronics (STMPA.PA) , BESI (BESI.AS) , Infineon (IFXGn.DE) et ASMI (ASMI.AS) reculant de 5,3% à 8,3%. Legrand (LEGD.PA) et Schneider Electric (SCHN.PA) , dont l'activité est très dépendante des centres de données, enregistrent des baisses respectives de 4,2 et de 3,7% à Paris. Dans le reste de l'actualité des entreprises, Pernod Ricard (PERP.PA) avance légèrement (+0,97%) après avoir fait état d'une baisse moins importante que prévu de son chiffre d'affaires du premier trimestre. TotalEnergies (TTEF.PA) , qui a déclaré s'attendre à ce que son bénéfice du troisième trimestre soit porté par un quasi-quadruplage des marges de raffinage et par une forte hausse des revenus liés au gaz naturel liquéfié (GNL), prend 0,99%. Le fabricant d'équipements télécoms Ericsson (ERICb.ST) grimpe de plus de 9% après avoir publié un bénéfice d'exploitation trimestriel avec une baisse moins marquée qu'initialement anticipé. Tomtom (TOM2.AS) perd 2,88%, le spécialiste néerlandais de la cartographie numérique ayant annoncé son intention de réorganiser ses activités, ce qui affectera environ 200 postes dans le monde. TAUX Les rendements obligataires sont en nette baisse jeudi dans un contexte d'aversion au risque. Aux Etats-Unis, le rendement des Treasuries à dix ans perd 10,7 points de base à 5,0829% et est en passe d'enregistrer sa plus forte baisse journalière depuis début août 2025. Celui du titre à deux ans recule de 6,8 points de base à 4,7340%. Dans la zone euro, le rendement du Bund allemand à dix ans cède 10 points de base à 3,3664%, celui de l'obligation à deux ans abandonne 6 points de base à 3,0401%. En France, le taux de rendement de l'OAT à dix ans perd 12,5 points de base pour s'établir à 4,7553%. Les anticipations concernant l'évolution des taux de la Banque centrale européenne (BCE) restent globalement inchangées, les marchés monétaires tablant sur un statu quo en octobre avant une nouvelle hausse en décembre. Selon Alvaro Santos Pereira, membre du conseil des gouverneurs de l'institution de Francfort, [USN:L6N4610KY TEXT:"l'inflation"] liée aux prix de l'énergie ne se répercute pas sur les autres prix, ce qui constitue un signe rassurant. Au Royaume-Uni, Huw Pill, chef économiste de la Banque d'Angleterre (BoE), [USN:L6N4610LI TEXT:"a dit"] jeudi qu'un possible relèvement des taux ne devait pas être interprété comme le début d'une longue série de hausses. La BoE devrait relever son taux directeur en novembre pour la première fois depuis plus de trois ans, le portant à 4%, selon la majorité des économistes interrogés par Reuters. CHANGES Le dollar recule jeudi par rapport à son plus haut niveau depuis 18 mois atteint la veille, la forte baisse des rendements des bons du Trésor pesant sur la devise américaine. Le billet vert perd 0,48% face à un panier de devises de référence (.DXY) , tandis que l'euro gagne 0,51% à 1,1213 dollar . PÉTROLE Les prix du pétrole évoluent sur de faibles variations, les investisseurs examinant les perspectives d'approvisionnement et les [USN:L6N4600N9 TEXT:"tensions persistantes"] au Moyen-Orient. Le Brent recule de 1,3% à 104,68 dollars le baril et le brut léger américain (West Texas Intermediate, WTI) 0,06% à 95,03 dollars. Les opérateurs analysent également les plans des Etats-Unis visant [USN:L6N461003 TEXT:"à alléger"] les sanctions contre les navires de la "flotte fantôme", qui transportent du pétrole en provenance de Russie, d'Iran ou du Venezuela, afin de faire baisser les taux de fret mondiaux. Les répercussions des perturbations du trafic maritime dans le détroit d'Ormuz commencent par ailleurs à se faire sentir sur les récoltes agricoles, menaçant de faire baisser les rendements et de faire grimper les prix des denrées alimentaires, [USN:L6N4610ND TEXT:"a déclaré"] jeudi à Reuters le directeur d'une agence des Nations unies chargée du développement rural. item.title: India's Tech Mahindra second-quarter revenue beats estimate
item.description: India's Tech Mahindra on Thursday beat second-quarter revenue expectations, helped by steady growth in its manufacturing and communications verticals and a weak rupee.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India's Tech Mahindra (TEML.NS) on Thursday beat second-quarter revenue expectations, helped by steady growth in its manufacturing and communications verticals and a weak rupee. The IT services company also said it would issue bonus shares worth up to 4.9 billion rupees, the first time it has done so since 2015. Consolidated revenue rose 15.6% to 161.80 billion rupees ($1.70 billion) year-on-year. Analysts, on average, expected revenue of 151.95 billion rupees, as per data compiled by LSEG. Analysts had expected Tech Mahindra to post one of the fastest revenue growth rates among large-cap IT services companies in the quarter, driven by large deal ramp-ups from clients including telecommunications provider Orange Business. The firm reported a 32.7% year-on-year rise in profit to 15.86 billion rupees, missing estimates of 17.08 billion rupees. The communications division's revenue, which accounts for a third of the Pune-based company's total, rose 9.5% year-on-year. Revenue from its manufacturing division, its second-largest, grew 7%. Revenue from the Tech Mahindra's banking and financial services segment, which the company has been pushing to expand in recent quarters, was up 4.6%. New deal wins in the quarter stood at $1.02 billion, up from $816 million in the same quarter last year. Larger peers [USN:L4N45U0R3 TEXT:"TCS"] (TCS.NS) and [USN:L4N45Y0P5 TEXT:"HCLTech"] (HCLT.NS) reported their results earlier in the month, while [USN:L4N4610ZD TEXT:"Wipro"] (WIPR.NS) reported higher quarterly revenue earlier in the day. item.title: Expana rebaja sus previsiones para la cosecha de maíz de la UE a un nuevo mínimo
item.description: Expana rebajó su previsión para la cosecha de maíz de la Unión Europea de este año, afectada por las olas de calor y la sequía del verano boreal, a un nuevo mínimo desde la década de los noventa, informó el jueves la empresa especializada en datos sobre materias primas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Expana rebajó su previsión para la cosecha de maíz de la Unión Europea de este año, afectada por las olas de calor y la sequía del verano boreal, a un nuevo mínimo desde la década de los noventa, informó el jueves la empresa especializada en datos sobre materias primas. La producción de maíz de la UE para la campaña 2026/27 se sitúa ahora en 44,9 millones de toneladas métricas, frente a los 46,2 millones previstos el mes pasado. Expana había señalado que su previsión anterior marcaba el nivel más bajo desde 1992, pero no ofreció una comparación con respecto a su nueva proyección. Los datos de la Organización de las Naciones Unidas para la Alimentación y la Agricultura (FAO) revelaron que la nueva estimación representaría la cifra más baja desde 1990. Se espera que el déficit de producción reduzca el uso de maíz en la alimentación del ganado en la UE durante la campaña 2026/27 en 8 millones de toneladas, es decir, un 13,5%, en comparación con el promedio de los últimos cinco años, según Expana. La UE también dependerá de importantes importaciones de maíz, y la interrupción de los envíos procedentes de Ucrania —su principal proveedor— a causa de la guerra supone un reto adicional, señaló. A pesar de la disponibilidad de suministros procedentes de Estados Unidos y Brasil, la UE podría seguir necesitando 11 millones de toneladas de maíz ucraniano, más que los 9,1 millones que importó de Ucrania la temporada pasada, según sus previsiones. En cuanto al trigo blando, el principal cultivo cerealístico de la UE, Expana mantuvo sin cambios su estimación de producción para la campaña 2026/27 en 126,1 millones de toneladas, lo que supone un descenso del 8% con respecto a la temporada pasada.

item.title: Why are credit default swaps unnerving AI investors?
item.description: The cost of insuring against the risk of potential US tech defaults has hit record levels in the latest sign of credit stress building in the so-called AI trade, especially for data centres dependent on future revenue.
item.dc:creator: Amanda Cooper
item.content:encoded: The cost of insuring against the risk of potential US tech defaults has hit record levels in the latest sign of credit stress building in the so-called AI trade, especially for data centres dependent on future revenue. Although shares in companies driving the AI boom are still among the biggest gainers on global equity markets this year, many have [USN:L6N4601B1 TEXT:"fallen"] sharply in the past few weeks, as investors reassess the cost of capital against a backdrop of rising [USN:L1N45A09M TEXT:"interest rates"] and [USN:L1N45Z121 TEXT:"inflation"]. There are also doubts among some investors and analysts about when, and in some cases, if, the billions of dollars pouring into data centres, computer power and other infrastructure will pay off. Demand for AI-linked credit default swaps (CDS), a form of insurance against default that gained prominence during the 2008 financial crisis, meanwhile has [USN:L1N46104Z TEXT:"surged"], even for heavyweights like Apple (AAPL.O) , Amazon (AMZN.O) and Microsoft (MSFT.O) . For some of their more heavily indebted competitors, suppliers and customers the cost of CDS has risen even faster. WHAT IS A CDS? A derivative that provides protection against the risk that a bond issuer, whether a company or government, fails to meet its debt obligations. Bond investors expect to receive interest payments and repayment of principal when a bond matures, but they bear the risk that those payments may not be made. Buying CDS helps investors hedge that risk by effectively providing insurance against a default or other credit event. If the value of a bond drops for any reason, an investor might add to their CDS holdings to help offset that, for example. None of the companies whose CDS have risen recently have defaulted on their obligations or signalled that they may do so. IS THIS A BIG MARKET? The market for single-name CDS, which cover the bonds of a single issuer, is worth about $9 trillion, the International Swaps and Derivatives Association (ISDA) said. That is a small portion of global bond markets, which have more than $150 trillion of debt securities outstanding, Bank for International Settlements data shows. The biggest CDS market is for government debt. Average daily CDS trading across the market was $16 billion in the second quarter, up from $13 billion a year earlier, the most recent data from the Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation shows. Saudi Arabia is the most actively traded. But average daily trades, even for large companies, can sometimes be in the single digits, meaning small transactions can have an outsized impact on prices. WHO BUYS CDS? Bond investors typically buy CDS through an intermediary, often an investment bank, which then finds a financial firm to issue an insurance policy on the bonds. These are "over-the-counter" deals that do not go through a central clearing house. Hedge funds also [USN:L4N3WQ17U TEXT:"participate in the market"], selling CDS to investors seeking to hedge exposure. The buyer pays a fee, called a premium, at regular intervals to the seller, which assumes the risk of a credit event. CDS are quoted as a credit spread, which is the number of basis points (bps) that the seller of the derivative charges the buyer for providing protection. The higher the perceived risk of a credit event, the wider the spread. A CDS quoted at 100 bps costs $1 annually to insure every $100 of debt. WHAT'S GOING ON WITH TECH CDS? CDS for [USN:L4N4601XL TEXT:"CoreWeave"] (CRWV.O) , a heavily indebted data centre operator at the eye of the current storm, have risen above 1,000 bps, S&P Global Market Intelligence data show. They suggest a roughly 63% chance of a default over the next five years, up from around 30% a year ago. Tech CDS moves reflect investor concern over how quickly massive investments in AI will translate into profits, and whether heavily indebted companies can generate returns fast enough to service mounting interest costs. Oracle (ORCL.N) has seen its CDS trade at nearly 300 bps, well above those of other AI-linked companies. Nvidia (NVDA.O) CDS have also risen sharply in recent weeks to around 90 bps, Meta CDS (META.O) are trading around 104 bps. By comparison, an index of investment-grade CDS is trading around 60 bps . WHAT TRIGGERS A CDS PAYOUT? A CDS pays out following a credit event, which can include a bankruptcy or a failure by an issuer to make bond payments. When concerns about an issuer's creditworthiness increase, demand for protection typically rises, widening CDS spreads. Payouts are not a given. When Swiss lender Credit Suisse collapsed and was taken over by rival UBS in 2023, the EMEA Credit Derivatives Determinations Committee (CDDC) ruled that event would not trigger a CDS payout. IF IT'S INSURANCE, WHAT'S THE PROBLEM? CDS provide a hedge for bondholders. But rising perceived risk pushes up the cost of protection, which can prompt investors to sell bonds and raise borrowing costs for issuers. That can amplify concerns about creditworthiness and potentially create a self-reinforcing cycle.

item.title: Superficie dedicada al trigo blando en la UE podría reducirse un 2% en próxima cosecha, dice Expana
item.description: La superficie cosechada de trigo blando en la Unión Europea el próximo año disminuiría un 2% en comparación con la cosecha de 2026, ya que los agricultores se enfrentan a unos costos de producción cada vez mayores, informó el jueves la empresa de datos sobre materias primas Expana.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La superficie cosechada de trigo blando en la Unión Europea el próximo año disminuiría un 2% en comparación con la cosecha de 2026, ya que los agricultores se enfrentan a unos costos de producción cada vez mayores, informó el jueves la empresa de datos sobre materias primas Expana. Aunque no facilitó una cifra concreta de superficie, la estimación porcentual sugiere que la superficie dedicada al trigo blando descendería hasta unos 21 millones de hectáreas, frente a los 21,4 millones de hectáreas que Expana estimó para la cosecha de este año. En un informe, la empresa señaló que "las previsiones de siembra de trigo blando no parecen prometedoras, ya que las perspectivas se ven lastradas por los elevados costos de producción". Los agricultores se han enfrentado a unos costos cada vez mayores de la energía y los fertilizantes, impulsados por las perturbaciones causadas por la guerra de Irán. No obstante, la necesidad de sustituir algunos cultivos de colza afectados por la sequía podría contribuir a mantener la superficie dedicada al trigo blando, añadió. En sus previsiones iniciales sobre la siembra de cereales en la UE, también anticipó que la superficie dedicada a la cebada de invierno se ampliaría a expensas de la cebada de primavera, mientras que se esperaba que la superficie dedicada al maíz siguiera disminuyendo.

item.title: Enrique y su esposa Meghan hacen su primera aparición conjunta desde su regreso al Reino Unido
item.description: El príncipe Enrique y su esposa Meghan aparecieron juntos en público el jueves por primera vez desde que regresaron por sorpresa a Gran Bretaña, volviendo a la ciudad donde realizaron su primer compromiso oficial conjunto hace nueve años.
item.dc:creator: Hannah McKay, Vitalii Yalahuzian
item.content:encoded: El príncipe Enrique y su esposa Meghan aparecieron juntos en público el jueves por primera vez desde que regresaron por sorpresa a Gran Bretaña, volviendo a la ciudad donde realizaron su primer compromiso oficial conjunto hace nueve años. Harry, el hijo menor del rey Carlos, y Meghan sorprendieron al monarca y al resto de la familia real cuando se trasladaron de California a Inglaterra hace dos meses con sus hijos, el príncipe Archie, de 7 años, y la princesa Lilibet, de 5. En su primera aparición pública conjunta desde entonces, la pareja regresó a Nottingham, en el centro de Inglaterra, ciudad que ya visitaron en 2017, poco después de que se anunciara su boda. Comenzaron visitando un estudio de grabación gestionado por una organización benéfica juvenil y comunitaria que ha recibido el apoyo de una donación de 1,1 millones de libras (1,46 millones de dólares) anunciada por Enrique el año pasado. Más tarde tenían previsto visitar una organización benéfica que lucha contra la pobreza alimentaria, dirigida por un grupo llamado Himmah, a la que Meghan donó 10.000 libras procedentes de las ventas de un libro de cocina publicado para recaudar fondos tras el incendio de la Torre Grenfell de Londres. El programa de actividades concluye con una visita a otra organización benéfica a la que la pareja ha prestado su apoyo, dedicada a los jóvenes y vinculada a su anterior visita en 2017. DIVISIÓN EN LA OPINIÓN PÚBLICA Harry y Meghan, el duque y la duquesa de Sussex, se han convertido en figuras profundamente polarizantes desde que renunciaron a sus obligaciones reales para mudarse a California en 2020, y han vertido críticas mordaces tanto contra la familia del príncipe como contra la propia institución real. Las encuestas de opinión muestran que la mayoría de los británicos tiene una opinión negativa de ellos, aunque los jóvenes se muestran mucho más comprensivos. En su visita a Nottingham hace nueve años, fueron recibidos por una gran multitud que agitaba banderas y les aclamaba. La visita del jueves fue un acto mucho más discreto, pero la pareja charló con unos 100 escolares emocionados y simpatizantes, a los que se unieron numerosos medios de comunicación. Meghan se mostró emocionada cuando una mujer le entregó un gran ramo de flores y le dio un abrazo. "Solo queríamos apoyarte", le dijo otra simpatizante. "Queríamos estar aquí… lo entendemos, queríamos que supieras que te hemos mostrado mucho cariño". Cuando Enrique hizo su primera aparición pública en solitario desde su traslado, declaró que era "bueno estar de vuelta en suelo británico", pero su regreso no ha estado exento de dificultades. La ubicación de su nuevo hogar se ha mantenido en secreto por motivos de seguridad y no viven en una residencia real. Tuvieron que cambiar a sus hijos de colegio poco después de que comenzara el curso por motivos de seguridad, y el portavoz de la pareja también condenó las acciones de "ciertos paparazzi europeos" que se entrometían en su intimidad.

item.title: Deutscher Reederverband alarmiert - Bessere Sicherung von Seewegen
item.description: Angesichts der wachsenden Bedrohungen für die Handelsschifffahrt fordern Deutschlands Reeder von der Politik mehr Einsatz zur Sicherung der Seewege. "Wir sind an einem Punkt angelangt, an dem die gleichzeitige Eskalation auf mehreren zentralen Seewegen die regelbasierte Ordnung auf See insgesamt gefährdet. Angriffe auf zivile Schiffe und die Blockade freier Durchfahrten dürfen nicht zur Normalität werden", erklärte der Hauptgeschäftsführer des Verbands Deutscher Reeder (VDR), Martin Kröger, am Donnerstag. "Die Staatengemeinschaft muss dieser Entwicklung gemeinsam entgegenwirken - mit Diplomatie, internationaler Zusammenarbeit und wirksamem Schutz für Handelsschiffe und ihre Besatzungen."
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Angesichts der wachsenden Bedrohungen für die Handelsschifffahrt fordern Deutschlands Reeder von der Politik mehr Einsatz zur Sicherung der Seewege. "Wir sind an einem Punkt angelangt, an dem die gleichzeitige Eskalation auf mehreren zentralen Seewegen die regelbasierte Ordnung auf See insgesamt gefährdet. Angriffe auf zivile Schiffe und die Blockade freier Durchfahrten dürfen nicht zur Normalität werden", erklärte der Hauptgeschäftsführer des Verbands Deutscher Reeder (VDR), Martin Kröger, am Donnerstag. "Die Staatengemeinschaft muss dieser Entwicklung gemeinsam entgegenwirken - mit Diplomatie, internationaler Zusammenarbeit und wirksamem Schutz für Handelsschiffe und ihre Besatzungen." Wie nah die Gewalt inzwischen an Europa heranreiche, zeigten die jüngsten Angriffe auf Handelsschiffe im Schwarzen Meer. Der VDR bezog sich darauf, dass vor der Küste Bulgariens Frachtschiffe von Drohnen getroffen worden waren und eines der Schiffe sank. Inzwischen wurden nach Angaben Rumäniens auch vor dessen Küste zwei Schiffe von Drohnen getroffen. Sowohl Bulgarien als auch Rumänien sind Nato- und EU-Länder. Der VDR verwies zudem auf wiederholte Angriffe im Persischen Golf und rund um die Straße von Hormus sowie auf weiterhin drohende Attacken von Huthi-Rebellen im Roten Meer. "Die Folgen treffen unsere auf Rohstoffimporte angewiesene Wirtschaft ebenso wie uns Verbraucher beim Heizen, im Supermarkt oder an der Tankstelle. Sichere Seewege sind Grundlage unseres Wohlstandes und einer bezahlbaren Versorgung", sagte Kröger. Risiken für wichtige Handelsverbindungen gebe es auch durch Spannungen um Taiwan. "Vor der deutschen Haustür in der Ostsee erschweren zudem Störungen und Manipulationen von Satellitennavigationssignalen wie GPS die sichere Navigation." Trotz der angespannten Lage bleibe die Seeschifffahrt verlässlich, erklärte der Branchenverband. Reedereien und Besatzungen hielten die Versorgung mit angepassten Routen und langen Umwegen aufrecht. "Dass Waren weiterhin ankommen, darf nicht darüber hinwegtäuschen, wie gefährdet ihre Lieferwege inzwischen sind. Den höchsten Preis zahlen Seeleute, die bei Angriffen verletzt oder getötet werden", betonte Kröger. "Seewege schützen sich nicht von allein. Die Menschen, die unsere Versorgung sichern, brauchen selbst Sicherheit." Der VDR appelliere deshalb an die Bundesregierung und Partner, die diplomatischen Bemühungen zur Beendigung der Angriffe zu verstärken, freie Durchfahrten zu sichern und Schutzmaßnahmen zu koordinieren. Dazu gehören auch ausreichend ausgestattete Marinen und Schutzmissionen wie Aspides.

item.title: CoreWeave shares, bonds slide further as AI debt fears mount
item.description: AI cloud firm CoreWeave's shares and bonds slumped further on Thursday despite CEO assurances about its strong deal backlog, in one of the deepest crises of investor confidence yet in an AI build-out increasingly fueled by borrowing.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: AI cloud firm CoreWeave's (CRWV.O) shares and bonds slumped further on Thursday despite CEO assurances about its strong deal backlog, in one of the deepest crises of investor confidence yet in an AI build-out increasingly fueled by borrowing. The company's stock fell 6% in premarket trading after a more than 15% drop on Wednesday, among the biggest decliners in a global tech stocks rout. The yield on its April-issued bonds due 2031 surged past 16%, above the level that typically signals distress, drawing a "yikes" from Elon Musk on social media. Loss-making CoreWeave, which has around $50 billion in debt, has in recent days become the focus of growing doubts about whether the tech industry can sustain a data center boom that is saddling newer cloud firms with heavy borrowing and straining cash flow even at giants such as Google-owner Alphabet. The cost of insuring the Nvidia-backed company's debt against default has climbed to around 1,000 basis points, a level that implies a nearly 63% chance the company defaults within five years, up from about 30% a year ago. CoreWeave leads a group of newer cloud providers known as neoclouds, which rent out computing power from tight in supply and costly Nvidia processors to meet the tech industry's soaring demand, often leaning on borrowing to fund the chip purchases. Critics say that leaves such firms exposed to any cooling in AI demand, while the chips lose value as newer generations arrive, forcing another round of heavy spending to replace them. CoreWeave, which in August raised its annual capital spending forecast by $4 billion to between $35 billion and $39 billion, is expected to post revenue of nearly $13 billion this year and a loss of $2.13 billion, according to analysts' estimates. Growing worries about the build-out, on which US tech giants are expected to spend more than $700 billion this year, have in recent days rippled through the stocks that have been the market's biggest winners since ChatGPT's November 2022 launch. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, a closely watched gauge of semiconductor stocks, has erased over $1.6 trillion in market value in an 11.6% slide over the past six sessions. The tech-heavy Nasdaq has declined more than 3% in the period. On Thursday, tech shares fell across Asia, Europe and the US, dragging broader markets lower on fears that high and rising interest rates could bring a reckoning for the sector. CoreWeave's neocloud rivals such as Nebius (NBIS.O) , Applied Digital (APLD.O) and Iren (IREN.O) fell between 3.2% and 5%. 'UNLIMITED' POOLS OF CAPITAL The CoreWeave sell-off came as its co-founder Brannin McBee told the Financial Times the company was seeking an investment-grade rating that would open the door to "unlimited" capital. On the same day, research firm Gartner said that about 80% of neoclouds could shut down by 2030, and that more than $3.5 trillion of AI infrastructure spending could face impairment if AI providers keep up their current pace of investment. "In 2026, AI providers are expected to spend nearly $1 trillion on AI infrastructure, and are forecast to invest an additional $6 trillion between 2027 and 2030,” said Will Sommer, analyst at Gartner. "However, our research indicates enterprise and consumer AI revenue will be insufficient to support profitable returns on all planned AI capital expenditures during this period.” CoreWeave CEO Mike Intrator pushed back on the concerns in an internal memo on Wednesday seen by Reuters, telling employees the company's deal backlog more than covers its debt obligations and that markets can sometimes "misunderstand and act irrationally." (This story has been refiled to fix the dateline to Oct 15 from Oct 14.)

item.title: Fintech startup Ramp hits $60 billion valuation after $1.85 billion funding round
item.description: Financial technology startup Ramp said on Thursday it had raised $1.85 billion in a primary financing round led by Dragoneer Investment Group, valuing the company at $60 billion, as the company expands its artificial intelligence offerings.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Financial technology startup Ramp said on Thursday it had raised $1.85 billion in a primary financing round led by Dragoneer Investment Group, valuing the company at $60 billion, as the company expands its artificial intelligence offerings. The funding underscores growing investor interest in financial automation, as corporate software companies add artificial intelligence to expense management, procurement and treasury functions once dominated by legacy enterprise players. Ramp's valuation marks a rise from [USN:L4N42C0YI TEXT:"$44 billion in June"], when it raised $750 million in a funding round. The New York-based company, which provides corporate cards and expense management software, said it generates more than $2 billion in annualized revenue and has positive cash flow. Founded in 2019, Ramp serves more than 85,000 companies, which collectively account for more than $275 billion in annualized purchase volume, up 175% from a year earlier. The company is also expanding into artificial intelligence tools, including software to monitor AI spending and optimize the cost of running AI models. The latest round was co-led by Thrive Capital, Founders Fund, Sands Capital and Avenir Growth. Other investors included Fidelity Management & Research Company, T. Rowe Price, GIC and Coatue, the company said. Ramp said it has raised approximately $5 billion in total equity financing, including the latest round.

item.title: Swedish parliament votes against Social Democrats leader as PM, as expected
item.description: Sweden's parliament on Thursday rejected Social Democrats leader Magdalena Andersson's bid to form a minority government, as widely expected, extending a period of uncertainty over who will become prime minister after last month's general election.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Sweden's parliament on Thursday rejected Social Democrats leader Magdalena Andersson's bid to form a minority government, [USN:L6N45K0F0 TEXT:"as widely expected"], extending a [USN:L8N4590Y1 TEXT:"period of uncertainty"] over who will become prime minister after last month's general election. Four centre-left opposition parties, which have all said they favour Andersson as prime minister, on September 13 [USN:L1N455016 TEXT:"won a majority"] of seats in Sweden's parliament, the Riksdag, but do not agree on who should be part of a new government. The opposition in September won 176 seats to 173 for Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson's right-wing bloc. Thursday's ballot was [USN:L6N45Z0LR TEXT:"the first"] of up to four votes before a new election must be called "It's been clear to me since the election night that it will take some time and that several ballots would likely be necessary to appoint a prime minister," Andersson told reporters after the vote in parliament Only the Social Democrats voted in favour of Andersson, while the other parties voted against The parliament speaker is widely expected to next ask Kristersson of the Moderates -- the second-biggest party after the Social Democrats -- to have a go at forming a government There is little indication so far that Kristersson would be able to secure a majority, and the task of government formation could thus revert to Andersson at a later time

item.title: UK comedian Russell Brand's accuser told police she blamed herself for alleged rape
item.description: One of six women who allege British actor and comedian Russell Brand sexually assaulted them over a decade broke down in tears as she told police she blamed herself for being raped by him more than 25 years ago, his trial heard on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Sam Tobin
item.content:encoded: One of six women who allege British actor and comedian Russell Brand sexually assaulted them over a decade broke down in tears as she told police she blamed herself for being raped by him more than 25 years ago, his trial heard on Thursday. Brand, once one of Britain's most high-profile broadcasters and the former husband of US singer Katy Perry, is on trial accused of three counts of rape, three of sexual assault and one of indecent assault between 1999 and 2009. The 51-year-old denies the allegations and told police after his arrest that he had never engaged in non-consensual sexual activity. Prosecutors on Wednesday described him as being a ruthless sexual predator as his career progressed from stand-up comedy gigs to becoming a TV presenter and later a Hollywood movie star. On the second day of his trial at London's Southwark Crown Court, jurors were played a police interview with a woman who says she met Brand at an event at the Labour Party conference in 1999, before he raped her in her hotel room. "He knew what he was doing... he wanted to have sex that night and I was there," the woman said. "I just remember him pushing me and I said 'no', but I was really scared ... I can't remember much after that." She said a 2023 documentary, which made allegations of sexual misconduct against Brand, prompted her to contact police, adding: "I saw how manipulative he was ... I was thinking this is what he did to me but in a different way." The woman also said: "I know I said 'no' ... I knew I couldn't get out of the situation. 'Do I shout, do I scream?'" She told police that she felt that "this is something dirty that happened to me ... and I thought it was my fault", adding: "But in those days it was your fault, you know?" The woman also said Brand had been "almost like trying to convince me it was all OK". She described it as "what abusers do". Brand told her afterwards "don't worry, I get tested regularly", she added, and wrote his email address down for her. 'VORACIOUS' DESIRE Prosecutor Riel Karmy-Jones [USN:L8N4600OQ TEXT:"said on Wednesday"] that Brand's "strong desire for some form of sexual contact was indiscriminate and voracious". Brand is alleged to have tried to drag a woman into a toilet cubicle at MTV Europe where she worked in 2001 and separately to have orally raped a woman in a toilet cubicle in a bar in 2004. He is also charged with indecently assaulting a woman in 2004 or 2005, anally raping a fifth complainant after they had consensual sex at his home in 2009, and later that same year sexually assaulting a woman who worked for Channel 4. All six complainants, who are legally entitled to lifelong anonymity, came forward after the 2023 documentary, Judge Joel Bennathan told jurors on Thursday. He said the women whose allegations were featured in the documentary were not part of the trial and their accusations had not been tested in court. He added: "The defence may suggest the programme caused the complainants, or at least some of them, to revisit historic sexual events and in their memories twist them from the consensual acts they were to the crimes they now allege." The trial is expected to last around six weeks.

item.title: Prince Harry and wife Meghan make first joint appearance since UK return
item.description: Prince Harry and his wife Meghan appeared together in public on Thursday for the first time since they made a surprise return to Britain, returning to the city where they made their maiden joint official engagement nine years ago.
item.dc:creator: Hannah McKay, Vitalii Yalahuzian
item.content:encoded: Prince Harry and his wife Meghan appeared together in public on Thursday for the first time since they made a [USN:L8N44N0XA TEXT:"surprise return to Britain"], returning to the city where they made their maiden joint official engagement nine years ago. Harry, the younger son of King Charles, and Meghan shocked the monarch and other members of the royal family when they relocated from California to England two months ago with their children Prince Archie, 7, and Princess Lilibet, 5. In their first joint public outing since then, the couple returned to Nottingham in central England which they visited in 2017, shortly after it was announced they were getting married. They began by visiting a recording studio run by a youth and community charity which has received support from a [USN:L5N3UW0YL TEXT:"£1.1 million ($1.46 million) donation"] announced by Harry last year. Later they were to visit a charity which tackles food poverty run by a group called Himmah to which Meghan donated £10,000 from sales of a cookbook released to raise funds in the wake of London's Grenfell Tower fire disaster. The engagements conclude with a visit to another charity the couple have backed which supports young people and is linked to their previous visit in 2017. HARRY AND MEGHAN DIVIDE PUBLIC OPINION Harry and Meghan, the Duke and Duchess of Sussex, have become deeply polarising figures since they stepped down from royal duties to move to California in 2020, going on to deliver scathing criticism of both the prince's family and the royal institution itself. Opinion polls show a majority of Britons hold a negative opinion of them, although young people are far more sympathetic. On their visit to Nottingham nine years ago they were met by large flag-waving cheering crowds. Thursday's visit was a much lower-key affair, but the couple chatted with about 100 excited schoolchildren and well-wishers joined by large numbers of media. Meghan looked emotional as one woman handed her a large bouquet of flowers and gave her a hug. "We just wanted to support you," another well-wisher told her. "We wanted to be here ... we understand, we wanted you to know that we've shown you so much love." When Harry made [USN:L1N4590X0 TEXT:"his first solo public appearance"] since their relocation he declared it was "good to be back on British soil" but their return has not been without difficulties. The location of their new home has been kept private amid security concerns and they are not living in a royal residence. They had to [USN:L8N45M0NT TEXT:"move their children"] to a new school not long after they started term because of concerns about security, with the couple's spokesperson also condemning the actions of "certain European paparazzi" intruding into their privacy. ($1 = 0.7549 pounds)

item.title: Roumanie-Deux bateaux en feu en mer Noire, sept marins portés disparus
item.description: Des équipes de secours roumaines sont à la recherche de sept membres d'équipage d'un des deux chimiquiers qui ont pris feu jeudi à la limite des eaux territoriales de la Roumanie en mer Noire, incident qui coïncide avec la détection d'une présence de drones russes dans l'espace aérien roumain, ont dit les autorités du pays.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Des équipes de secours roumaines sont à la recherche de sept membres d'équipage d'un des deux chimiquiers qui ont pris feu jeudi à la limite des eaux territoriales de la Roumanie en mer Noire, incident qui coïncide avec la détection d'une présence de drones russes dans l'espace aérien roumain, ont dit les autorités du pays. Le président roumain Nicusor Dan a déclaré que deux navires avaient été touchés par les drones, refusant de préciser si ceux-ci étaient russes. "Deux drones aériens les ont frappés", a-t-il dit à des journalistes à Bruxelles, en marge d'un sommet de l'Union européenne. "Il y aura une réaction de l'Etat roumain", a-t-il affirmé, ajoutant être dans l'attente d'informations supplémentaires. Les deux navires étaient ancrés près de l'embouchure du canal de Sulina, un bras du Danube qui se verse dans le mer Noire, devenu une voie de navigation majeure pour l'Ukraine depuis que la Russie a attaqué ses ports de mer Noire. L'un des navires se situait dans les eaux roumaines, l'autre juste à l'extérieur. La mer Noire et ses ports sont le théâtre d'attaques de plus en plus fréquentes dans le cadre de la stratégie d'asphyxie économique de l'adversaire tentée aussi bien par la Russie que par l'Ukraine, plus de quatre ans et demi après le début de l'invasion russe à grande échelle de l'Ukraine. Depuis le début du mois, cinq navires commerciaux ont ainsi été [USN:L8N45Z11F TEXT:"touchés"] en mer Noire, au large des côtes de la Roumanie et de la Bulgarie, faisant un total de 23 morts ou disparus parmi les marins. À LA RECHERCHE DES MARINS DISPARUS Pour éviter ces attaques, l'Ukraine s'appuie de plus en plus sur ses ports fluviaux le long du Danube et sur des voies de navigation proches des côtes de la Bulgarie et de la Roumanie, deux pays membres de l'Union européenne et de l'Otan. Les autorités navales roumaines ont déclaré jeudi avoir reçu une alerte d'urgence provenant du chimiquier Wine Trader, battant pavillon de Saint-Marin, dont cinq des 12 membres d'équipage sont sains et saufs. Mercredi soir, un navire transportant des produits chimiques et pétroliers, battant pavillon comorien, a également pris feu et l'équipage, sain et sauf, a dû être évacué. Le ministère de l'Intérieur roumain a précisé avoir dépêché deux hélicoptères Black Hawk pour participer à la mission de recherche et de sauvetage, ainsi que deux navires avec du personnel médical à bord. "Pour l'instant, les opérations de sauvetage ne peuvent pas être menées en toute sécurité en raison de très hautes vagues", a-t-il ajouté dans le communiqué. La Roumanie partage une frontière de 614 km avec l'Ukraine, dont une grande partie longe le Danube. Elle a signalé des violations répétées de son espace aérien par des drones russes au cours des quatre dernières années. Lors de son arrivée au sommet européen qui se tient ce jeudi et vendredi à Bruxelles, le Premier ministre bulgare Roumen Radev a déclaré qu'un projet de moratoire sur les attaques de navires civils en mer Noire était au menu des discussions. "Aujourd'hui, nous allons discuter du moratoire proposé visant à mettre fin aux attaques contre les navires civils en mer Noire", a-t-il dit aux journalistes.

item.title: Israeli firm used online ads to run vast spy operation, researchers say
item.description: Discover-Tech used a sprawling network of online ads to track targets and help hack their devices.
item.dc:creator: Raphael Satter
item.content:encoded: Israeli digital advertising agency Discover-Tech spied on internet users through a sprawling network of online ads that it used to track targets and help hack their devices, two research groups said on Thursday. Its services gave Israel's Candiru — a spyware company [USN:L1N2RU186 TEXT:"blacklisted by the US government"] — as well as other Israeli surveillance firms access to advertising platforms run by Google (GOOGL.O) , Comcast (CMCSA.O) , Russia's Yandex and others, according to separate reports from Canadian cyber watchdog group Citizen Lab and New York advertising security firm Confiant. The reports show how the online advertising business, long a subject of privacy concerns, can also serve as a channel for sweeping espionage campaigns. "The way online advertising works today is a systemic security threat," Wolfie Cristl, a senior researcher at Citizen Lab, told Reuters. "For states, the private sector, civil society and everyone else alike."
